section_summary: These pages close one set of naval scrapping tables, then document September and October 1948 reports that the disposal of former Japanese warships was nearly complete. They also contain correspondence about classifying Japanese vessels used by the Korean Coast Guard and a December 1949 telegram reporting a Chinese press allegation that the United States planned to rebuild Japan’s navy.

subfiles.title: Scrapping program summaries for completely scrapped minor vessels and submarines
subfiles.about: Two concluding sheets list scrapping dates, scrap tonnage, and yards for minor vessels and submarines.
subfiles.summary: The tables continue an earlier report and total 22,808 tons of scrap from 67 minor ships and 7,233 tons from 35 submarines.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of press release concerning ship-scrapping program
subfiles.from: Acting United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Forwards a Far East Command release on progress in scrapping warships and salvaging merchant vessels.
subfiles.summary: Reports warship scrapping 97 percent complete and summarizes the separate merchant vessel program.

subfiles.title: Ship Scrapping Program Nearing Completion
subfiles.from: Public Information Office, General Headquarters, Far East Command
subfiles.about: Announces the status, costs, and expected completion of Japanese warship scrapping and merchant ship salvage.
subfiles.summary: States that 406 of 421 former warships had been scrapped, with the rest expected by year’s end. A table accounts for all 625 merchant vessels across salvage, scrapping, and total-loss categories.

subfiles.title: Classification and possible transfer of Japanese vessels used by the Korean Coast Guard
subfiles.from: Civil Affairs Division, citing State and Army Departments
subfiles.about: Requests a firm combatant classification for former Japanese minelayer-type tugs used by the Korean Coast Guard.
subfiles.summary: Explains that non-combatant status could simplify Korean retention, sale, or loan of the vessels and help prevent smuggling between Japan and Korea.

subfiles.title: Memorandum forwarding proposed cable on Korean Coast Guard vessels
subfiles.about: Seeks Army concurrence on a proposed cable asking whether the vessels are combatant or non-combatant.
subfiles.summary: Asks for Army concurrence and notes Major Lieding’s familiarity with the issue.

subfiles.title: Draft cable on transfer of vessels to the Korean Government
subfiles.about: Proposes asking SCAP to classify Japanese minelayer-type tugs before arranging their Korean disposition.
subfiles.summary: The heavily degraded draft cites an earlier ruling on naval tugs and suggests retention, sale, or loan for Korean Coast Guard use.

subfiles.title: Draft telegram to SCAP concerning Korean Coast Guard vessels
subfiles.about: Requests classification and comments on Japanese minelayer-type tugs proposed for Korean Coast Guard use.
subfiles.summary: Cites the May 1947 position that naval tugs, harbor craft, and salvage vessels were non-combatant. It outlines retention by U.S. forces in Korea, eventual sale, or a loan to the Korean government.

subfiles.title: Telegram on near completion of Japanese navy scrapping
subfiles.about: Reports Vice Admiral Berkey’s announcement that scrapping of Japan’s former navy was 98 percent complete.
subfiles.summary: Reports 415 of 422 units disposed of and about 200,000 tons of scrap recovered.

subfiles.title: Summary of program for scrapping Japanese former combatant vessels
subfiles.from: Acting United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Forwards November 1948 headquarters material showing the scrapping program virtually complete.
subfiles.summary: Transmits three copies of a memorandum and October cumulative scrapping summary.

subfiles.title: Scrapping Report Summary
subfiles.from: General Headquarters, Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: Distributes October 1948 scrapping summaries for former Japanese naval vessels.
subfiles.summary: Lists enclosed submarine, minor-vessel, and completed-ship summaries.

subfiles.title: Destruction of Ex-Japanese Combatant Vessels, October 1948
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: Forwards October scrapping summaries and photographs, identifying vessels completed or newly added.
subfiles.summary: Lists five vessels completed during October and two additions to the minor-vessel program.

subfiles.title: Scrapping Program Summary for Submarines
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: Records October submarine scrapping progress and completed totals.
subfiles.summary: Shows one submarine under salvage and 41 submarines plus 106 Kōryū craft completed.

subfiles.title: Scrapping Program Summary for Vessels of Destroyer Tonnage or Less
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: Records October progress for minor vessels and totals for completed ships.
subfiles.summary: Shows 119 completed minor ships and 97.65 percent of estimated scrap recovered across 126 ships.

subfiles.title: Scrapping Program Summary for Completely Scrapped Ships
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: Lists completed major ships, minor vessels, and submarines with disposal dates, scrap tonnage, and yards.
subfiles.summary: Five sheets catalogue 35 major ships, 119 minor ships, and 41 submarines plus 106 Kōryū craft. The tables include ships scrapped at Japanese yards and vessels abandoned or sunk.

subfiles.title: Telegram reporting Chinese press allegation about rebuilding Japan’s navy
subfiles.about: Relays a Chinese newspaper and news-agency claim that U.S. authorities sought cruisers for Japanese coastal defense.
subfiles.summary: Reports an allegation that 27 American cruisers loaned to the Soviet Union might be transferred to Japanese coastal defense forces.
